case_name: Smt. Vishwarupa Jain vs Dharmendra Jain
facts_of_case: The petitioner's application under Order 7 Rule 11 read with Order 2 Rule 2 of CPC was dismissed by the trial court. The respondent had filed a petition for judicial separation and later for divorce without mentioning any cause of action.

legal_principles.principle: A petition for divorce under Section 13(1A) of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 is not maintainable if there is no cause of action.
legal_principles.held: He further submits that during pendency of the first appeal before the High Court, respondent has filed a suit/petition on 24.09.2020 for divorce under section 13(1A) of the Hindu Marriage Act even without mentioning any cause of action, which cannot be said to have arisen prior to lapse of 7 years and as such the petition for divorce is not maintainable and deserves to be dismissed/rejected.

legal_principles.principle: A decree for judicial separation under Section 10 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 can be rescinded if it is considered just and reasonable to do so.
legal_principles.held: Where a decree for judicial separation has been passed, it shall no longer be obligatory for the petitioner to cohabit with the respondent, but the court may, on the application by petition of either party and on being satisfied of the truth of the statements made in such petition, rescind the decree if it considers it just and reasonable to do so.

outcome.final_order: The petition for divorce is not maintainable and deserves to be dismissed/rejected.
